newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates lower in week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates lower in week.

text.p: Mortgage rates fell this week to the lowest levels since December as signs that inflation remained in check convinced the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.65 percent in the week ending Feb. 14, down from 7.74 percent last week. The rate was the lowest since 7.64 percent in the week ended Dec. 27.
The 15-year loan rate fell to 7.14 percent from 7.25 percent, the lowest level since 7.06 percent in the week ended Dec. 13.
Adjustable mortgage rates rose to an average 5.52 percent from 5.51 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 6.94 percent, the 15-year loan 6.44 percent and the adjustable loan 5.19 percent.

"The Federal Reserve's action to leave monetary policy unchanged should help promote an affordable mortgage market over the next few weeks, in which case we expect to see a rebound in the (home sales) figures," Freddie Mac deputy chief economist Frank Nothaft said.
The Fed last week decided not to increase interest rates at its policy-making meeting, following a spate of recent data that showed steady economic growth with no inflationary pressure.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. Adjustable loan charges edged down to 1.3 percent from 1.4 percent.
